_comment: THE IN-PERIMETER ENTRIES OF THE IEA CCUS PROJECTS DATABASE 2026, worked one at a
time. 179 of the list's 425 European entries: 42 cement and 137 CO2 transport and
storage. The other 246 are refused by the perimeter on the publisher's own
Subsector and are DERIVED in sources/build_cement_ccs_benchmark.py rather than
listed here -- hand-listing 246 mechanical refusals would have invited a typo to
become a class.
KEYED BY THE IEA'S OWN `ID`, which is what the brief means by the benchmark's own
identifier. The key is a string because JSON keys are.
MATCHING TO A ROW IS BY COMPANY AND WORKS AGREEING, never by a name stem. That is
the batteries rule (sources/build_batteries_benchmark.py, 'MATCHING, AND WHAT IS
NOT A JOIN') and it is the only route used here. Every match is printed on every
run for confirmation. Where two objects look like one works and no source says so,
the pair goes to `reference_debts` and NOT into a join.
CAPACITY ON AN ADMITTED ROW IS THE OWNER'S FIGURE AT THE OWNER'S UNIT. Neither IEA
capacity column is ever written onto a row: 'Announced capacity' is the list's
claim and 'Estimated capacity by IEA' is the IEA's own computation through the
conversion factors on the workbook's Definitions tab. Where the two speakers
differ, the pair is recorded in `disagreements` and neither is reconciled.
A PHASE IS AN ENTRY. The IEA lists announced phases as separate rows with separate
IDs -- Viking CCS Phase 1/2/3, Northern Endurance 1/2/3, Aramis storage 1/2. The
gate sums to the list's entry count, so each phase takes its own class; where the
works is held here, every phase entry classes `held` and names the same row, on
the batteries precedent that one benchmark line over two held works is counted
once per LIST ENTRY and the reference is written onto the row.

202.question: The cement perimeter holds 'a capture project at a cement works, of any capture technology, company-confirmed' and sets no floor and no pilot clause. These four entries are capture at a cement works and are described by their own owners as pilot, demonstration or test installations. The batteries perimeter HAS a pilot clause and refuses a pilot unless the company states it as a phase of a commercial line; the cement perimeter has no such sentence, so nothing here settles them.
202.speaker: HeidelbergCement, own release of 1 February 2021
202.verbatim: it has been decided to build the LEILAC 2 demonstration installation for carbon capture at the HeidelbergCement cement plant in Hanover, Germany... an installation around four times as large will be operated in Hanover, which will capture 20% of the cement plant's capacity, corresponding to around 100,000 tonnes of CO2 per year
202.rule_would_need_to_say: Whether a demonstration installation integrated into an operating cement works clears the cement perimeter, and if a floor applies, what it is. LEILAC 2 is Under construction with FID 2022 and 100,000 t CO2/yr, which is larger than several entries this pass admitted without question.
202.note: SEE ALSO THE REFERENCE DEBT on Hanover: this entry and IEA 556 both name a cement works at Hanover under different owners, and no source read here says whether they are one works or two.

539.verbatim: KBR will provide FEED services for the initial stage of the project which aims to develop and deploy Carbon Clean's breakthrough modular carbon capture technology - CycloneCC - to initially capture 100 tonnes per day (TPD) of CO2 at the plant
539.rule_would_need_to_say: Whether a 100 t/day modular unit at a cement works is a capture project for this perimeter, AND whether two capture projects at one works are one row or two -- IEA 540 (CO2LLECT, 1.3 Mt) is at the same Ruedersdorf works and was admitted by this pass.
539.note: 100 t/day is about 36,500 t/yr if annualised, and this register does not annualise a figure its owner stated per day.

speakers.says: the row is `paused` on the company's own statement

disagreements.held: Recorded, not reconciled. A list that carries a paused project as planned is saying something about the list's own vintage and resolution, and the row keeps the company's word.

speakers.says: up to 1.5 million tons of CO2 annually from 2030

disagreements.held: The row takes the owner's figure. The list's is here. Air Liquide, the technology partner, states the same 1.5 Mt on its own release of 24 October 2024.

speakers.says: the capture installation at Cementownia Kujawy starts in 2027

disagreements.held: Four years apart on the same works. Recorded, not reconciled: the owner's page is the later reading and the list may be carrying an older vintage of the same plan, and nothing read here says which.

speakers.says: capture > 700 thousand t CO2 per year

disagreements.held: A BOUND AGAINST A POINT VALUE, and they are not the same kind of statement. The owner states a lower bound; the list states a number that satisfies it. The row carries the bound as the owner made it.

speakers.says: about 90 per cent of the works' roughly 500,000 t CO2 annual emissions, after the final expansion stage

disagreements.held: The list's 0.8 Mt exceeds the works' own stated total emissions of about 0.5 Mt. Recorded as a disagreement rather than resolved, and no capture capacity is written onto the row.

speakers.says: an estimated 2 million tons of near-zero cement per annum from 2032

disagreements.held: NOT A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT A NUMBER BUT ABOUT WHICH SUBSTANCE IS BEING COUNTED -- tonnes of cement against tonnes of CO2. Recorded here so a reader comparing the two does not read one as the other.

reference_debts.believed: capture at one works, Vicat's Montalieu-Vercieu cement plant, admitted once as vaia-montalieu-vercieu
reference_debts.missing: No source read says whether HyNoVi is a phase of VAIA, its predecessor, or a separate unit. Vicat's 2021 release has HyNoVi capturing 40 per cent of the works' CO2 with a 330 MW electrolyser into methanol; its 2025 release has VAIA capturing 1.2 Mt, nearly 100 per cent, into sequestration. Both are Vicat and both are Montalieu-Vercieu, and the company never states the relation.
reference_debts.needed: A Vicat page or permit naming both project names, or naming HyNoVi as superseded.

pair: IEA 202, 'Heidelberg Materials LEILAC 2' - a cement plant at Hanover, owner HeidelbergCement
IEA 556, 'Hover cement works Hannover phase 2' - a cement works at Hoever, owner Holcim Deutschland
reference_debts.believed: NOTHING IS BELIEVED HERE, WHICH IS THE POINT
reference_debts.missing: Two entries name a cement works at Hanover under two different owners. HeidelbergCement's 2021 release says LEILAC 2 was decided for 'the HeidelbergCement cement plant in Hanover'; Holcim Deutschland's 2026 release puts its test plant at 'Zementwerk Hoever, Niedersachsen'. Hoever is in the Hanover region. Either these are two works, or one of the two statements is about a works its speaker no longer owns, or LEILAC 2 moved. NO SOURCE READ HERE SETTLES IT, so the two entries are kept apart and neither is merged into the other.
reference_debts.needed: A source naming the operator of the Hoever works and the site of LEILAC 2 together, or a permit for either.

pair: IEA 539, 'Carbon Clean CEMEX Rudersdorf plant phase 1'
reference_debts.believed: two capture projects at one works, CEMEX's Ruedersdorf plant
reference_debts.missing: Both are CEMEX at Ruedersdorf and they are different technologies at different scales with different partners -- Carbon Clean's CycloneCC at 100 t/day, Linde's at 1.3 Mt/yr. Whether the first is a stage of the second or a separate installation is not stated by anyone read. 540 is admitted; 539 is held for ruling and is not merged into it.
reference_debts.needed: A CEMEX statement relating the two.

pair: IEA 1459, 'ECCO2-LH (Lighthouse) LafargeHolcim Carboneras cement factory phase 2'
reference_debts.believed: two entries at one works, Holcim Espana's Carboneras plant
reference_debts.missing: ECCO2-LH is a 2020 CCU pilot the IEA carries as Cancelled; CO2nscious is a 2025 capture entry the IEA carries as Planned. Whether the second replaces the first is stated nowhere read. Neither is admitted, so no row turns on it, and the pair is recorded so a later pass does not merge them on the shared works name.
reference_debts.needed: A Holcim Espana statement naming both.
